"…" end local name = htmlEscape(raw):gsub(" ", " ") local secs = showSecs and string.format(" %ds", rem) or "" table.insert(parts, string.format( [[<span style="background:%s;color:%s;font-weight:700">]] .. [[ %s%s </span>]], style.bg, style.fg, name, secs)) if i < n then table.insert(parts, "  ") end end table.insert(parts, [[</center>]]) icesus.hud.cooldownsRow:echo(table.concat(parts)) end
-- ============================================================= -- GMCP handlers. -- Field names must match adm/daemons/gmcp_d.c. -- Char.Vitals & Char.Maxstats use: hp, mana, moves, psp, maxhp, -- maxmana, maxmoves, maxpsp. -- ============================================================= -- ============================================================= -- Guild resources -- two GMCP sources, one strip on the vitals row. -- Char.Vitals carries the scalars a guild runs on (fury, vitae, -- ...) beside HP/SP/EP, every heartbeat. The server -- never announces which keys those are -- adding one -- is a row in a table on the player object -- so every -- key that is not a core pool is a guild scalar here, -- and a resource the server grows later needs no -- release. -- Char.Resources carries the structured ones: templar bonds, scion -- souls, charms, piety. Throttled server-side to one -- push per ten seconds, replaced wholesale on arrival; -- an empty payload means a block you were shown has -- gone away. -- The strip holds what a player watches mid-fight: the scalar, the -- four bond strengths with a filling / draining arrow, the active -- charm. Load and drain, the soul list and the nine deities are one -- `hud guild` (or a click on the strip) away, printed to the console. -- ============================================================= local CORE_VITALS = { hp = true, mana = true, moves = true, psp = true, maxhp = true, maxmana = true, maxmoves = true, maxpsp = true } local BOND_ORDER = { "air", "water", "fire", "earth" } -- The nine, in the order the server's piety daemon lists them, so the -- list never reshuffles between pushes. local PIETY_ORDER = { "earth", "water", "fire", "air", "nameless king", "nether", "ancestors", "spirits", "aetheria" } local ARROW_UP, ARROW_DOWN = "\226\150\178", "\226\150\188" -- U+25B2 / U+25BC local GUILD_PAD = 10 -- px each side of the strip's text local GUILD_TIP = "Click for bonds, souls, charm abilities and devotion (hud guild)"
-- A populated sub-table, or nil. FluffOS encodes an empty mapping as -- [], which Mudlet decodes to an empty table -- the same as no block. local function block(t, key) local b = type(t) == "table" and t[key] if type(b) == "table" and next(b) ~= nil then return b end return nil end
-- A guild number is an exact reading, not a gauge: a bond at 1420 must -- never print as 1.4k. local function fmtNum(n) return string.format("%d", math.floor(tonumber(n) or 0)) end
local function capitalise(s) s = tostring(s or "") return s:sub(1, 1):upper() .. s:sub(2) end
-- Sorted keys of a name -> number table, largest value first, ties by -- name -- the order a scion decides what to forge in. local function keysByValue(t) local keys = {} for k in pairs(t) do keys[#keys + 1] = tostring(k) end table.sort(keys, function(a, b) local va, vb = tonumber(t[a]) or 0, tonumber(t[b]) or 0 if va ~= vb then return va > vb end return a < b end) return keys end
-- What the strip draws, in order: { html = .., cells = .. } per chip. -- `level` is how far to compact when the row is too narrow for the -- full form: 1 shortens bond names to their initial, 2 also shortens -- the charm name, 3 drops the charm chip. The numbers are never -- touched -- a reading that is wrong is worse than one that is absent. function icesus.guildChips(level) level = tonumber(level) or 0 local g = icesus.state.guild local P = icesus.palette local GS = icesus.guildStyles local chips = {} local function chip(label, colour, value, arrow) local html = string.format( [[<span style="color:%s">%s</span> ]] .. [[<span style="color:%s;font-weight:700">%s</span>]], colour, htmlEscape(label), P.textBright, htmlEscape(value)) local cells = ucells(label) + 1 + ucells(value) if arrow then html = html .. string.format([[<span style="color:%s">%s</span>]], arrow.colour, arrow.glyph) cells = cells + 1 end chips[#chips + 1] = { html = html, cells = cells } end
local keys = {} for k in pairs(g.scalars or {}) do keys[#keys + 1] = k end table.sort(keys) for _, k in ipairs(keys) do chip(capitalise(k), GS[k] or GS.other, fmtNum(g.scalars[k])) end
-- Strength in the strip, with the arrow saying whether the bond is -- filling or draining this tick. Load and the drain figure itself -- are in the printout, where there is room to label them. local bonds = block(g.resources, "bonds") if bonds then for _, el in ipairs(BOND_ORDER) do local b = bonds[el] if type(b) == "table" then local drain = tonumber(b.drain) or 0 local arrow if drain > 0 then arrow = { glyph = ARROW_UP, colour = P.green } elseif drain < 0 then arrow = { glyph = ARROW_DOWN, colour = P.red } end local label = capitalise(el) if level >= 1 then label = label:sub(1, 1) end chip(label, GS[el] or GS.other, fmtNum(b.strength), arrow) end end end
-- Souls stay out of the strip: a live scion holds fifty-odd fragment -- kinds, and their sum answers no question a player has mid-fight. -- Vitae is the scion's live number, and it is already here. local charms = block(g.resources, "charms") if charms and level < 3 then local desc = type(charms.desc) == "string" and charms.desc or "" if desc ~= "" or block(charms, "abilities") then if desc == "" then desc = "active" end if level >= 2 and ucells(desc) > 7 then desc = uhead(desc, 6) .. ELLIPSIS end chip("Charm", GS.charm, desc) end end return chips end
-- Pixels the strip needs for these chips: the badge rows' cell -- arithmetic, plus padding, rounded up to 20 px so a number growing a -- digit does not reflow the gauges every heartbeat. local function stripWidth(chips) local cells = 0 for i, c in ipairs(chips) do cells = cells + c.cells + (i < #chips and 3 or 0) end local px = math.ceil(cells * fsz("vitals", 10) * 0.88) + GUILD_PAD * 2 return math.ceil(px / 20) * 20 end
function icesus.hasGuildDetail() local r = icesus.state.guild.resources if type(r) ~= "table" then return false end for _, v in pairs(r) do if type(v) == "table" and next(v) ~= nil then return true end end return false end
function icesus.refreshGuild() if not icesus.hud or not icesus.hud.guildStrip then return end local L = icesus.hudLayout() local P = icesus.palette local st = icesus.state.guild local strip = icesus.hud.guildStrip local bottom = icesus.hud.bottom
-- The strip may take half of the row beside the column; the gauges -- keep the rest. Past that it compacts, a step at a time, and as a -- last resort it is clamped and the ends of the row are lost. local mainW = 1600 if getMainWindowSize then local ok, mw = pcall(getMainWindowSize) if ok and tonumber(mw) then mainW = tonumber(mw) end end local budget = math.max(120, math.floor((mainW - L.R) / 2)) local chips, gw = {}, 0 for level = 0, 3 do chips = icesus.guildChips(level) if #chips == 0 then break end gw = stripWidth(chips) if gw <= budget then break end end if gw > budget then gw = budget end
-- The carry summary advertises the detail only while there is some. if icesus.hud.carryLabel then pcall(function() icesus.hud.carryLabel:setToolTip(icesus.hasGuildDetail() and GUILD_TIP or "") end) end
if #chips == 0 then if st.stripW ~= 0 then st.stripW = 0 pcall(function() strip:hide() end) pcall(function() bottom:resize(L.stripW, L.VITALS_H) end) end return end
if gw ~= st.stripW then st.stripW = gw pcall(function() strip:resize(gw, L.VITALS_H) end) pcall(function() strip:move("-" .. (L.guildRight + gw), "-" .. L.B) end) pcall(function() bottom:resize("100%-" .. (L.R + gw), L.VITALS_H) end) pcall(function() strip:show() end) end
local sep = string.format( [[<span style="color:%s"> · </span>]], P.borderBright) local parts = {} for _, c in ipairs(chips) do parts[#parts + 1] = c.html end strip:echo([[<center>]] .. table.concat(parts, sep) .. [[</center>]]) end
-- Lines of `name value` pairs, wrapped so a scion's fifty-odd soul -- kinds do not arrive as one console-wide sentence. Zeroes stay, -- dimmed: "no standing with the nether" is itself a reading. local function kvLines(items, width) local sep = " <grey>\194\183<reset> " local lines, cur, len = {}, {}, 0 for _, it in ipairs(items) do local plain = #it.key + 1 + #it.val if #cur > 0 and len + 3 + plain > width then lines[#lines + 1] = table.concat(cur, sep) cur, len = {}, 0 end if it.dim then cur[#cur + 1] = string.format("<grey>%s %s<reset>", it.key, it.val) else cur[#cur + 1] = string.format("%s <white>%s<reset>", it.key, it.val) end len = len + (#cur > 1 and 3 or 0) + plain end if #cur > 0 then lines[#lines + 1] = table.concat(cur, sep) end return lines end
local function kvItems(t, dimZero) local items = {} for _, k in ipairs(keysByValue(t)) do local v = tonumber(t[k]) or 0 items[#items + 1] = { key = k, val = fmtNum(v), dim = dimZero and v == 0 } end return items end
local INDENT = " "
function icesus.printGuildDetail() local r = icesus.state.guild.resources local any = false cecho("\n<cyan>Icesus guild resources<reset>\n")
-- Bonds: the same columns the in-game bond table prints, in the same -- order and with the same words, so a templar reading one is reading -- the other. local bonds = block(r, "bonds") if bonds then any = true cecho(" <yellow>Bonds<reset> <grey>element strength load drain<reset>\n") for _, el in ipairs(BOND_ORDER) do local b = bonds[el] if type(b) == "table" then local drain = tonumber(b.drain) or 0 local col = drain > 0 and "green" or (drain < 0 and "red" or "grey") cecho(string.format(INDENT .. "%-12s %8s %6s <%s>%s%s<reset>\n", el, fmtNum(b.strength), fmtNum(b.load), col, drain > 0 and "+" or "", fmtNum(drain))) end end cecho(INDENT .. "<grey>drain is the net change each ten-second tick: " .. "positive fills the bond, negative empties it<reset>\n") end
local souls = block(r, "souls") if souls then any = true local items = kvItems(souls, true) cecho(string.format(" <yellow>Souls<reset> <grey>%d kind%s, largest first<reset>\n", #items, #items == 1 and "" or "s")) for _, line in ipairs(kvLines(items, 70)) do cecho(INDENT .. line .. "\n") end end
local charms = block(r, "charms") if charms then local desc = type(charms.desc) == "string" and charms.desc or "" local abil = block(charms, "abilities") if desc ~= "" or abil then any = true cecho(string.format(" <yellow>Charm<reset> <white>%s<reset>\n", desc ~= "" and desc or "active")) if abil then for _, line in ipairs(kvLines(kvItems(abil, false), 70)) do cecho(INDENT .. line .. "\n") end end end end
local piety = block(r, "piety") if piety then any = true local seen, items = {}, {} local function add(k) local v = tonumber(piety[k]) or 0 items[#items + 1] = { key = k, val = fmtNum(v), dim = (v == 0) } seen[k] = true end for _, k in ipairs(PIETY_ORDER) do if piety[k] ~= nil then add(k) end end local rest = {} for k in pairs(piety) do if not seen[k] then rest[#rest + 1] = tostring(k) end end table.sort(rest) for _, k in ipairs(rest) do add(k) end cecho(" <yellow>Devotion<reset> <grey>your standing with the nine<reset>\n") for _, line in ipairs(kvLines(items, 70)) do cecho(INDENT .. line .. "\n") end end
if not any then cecho(" <grey>Nothing to show \226\128\148 your character carries no guild " .. "resources or devotion right now.<reset>\n") end end
-- `hud guild`, and a click on the strip or the carry summary. Ask the -- server for a fresh Char.Resources, then print when it lands. The -- server throttles its own pushes to one every ten seconds because -- building the payload reaches three daemons; an explicit request -- clears that throttle, and the moment someone is actually reading -- the numbers is the moment worth spending it. The cooldown here only -- stops a repeated command from becoming a poll -- inside it, the -- last push is printed as is. icesus.GUILD_REFRESH_S = 2 function icesus.guildCommand() local st = icesus.state.guild local now = os.time() if isConnected and isConnected() and (now - (st.requestedAt or 0)) >= icesus.GUILD_REFRESH_S then st.requestedAt = now st.printPending = true sendGMCP("Char.Resources") -- A server that has never heard of the package answers nothing; -- print what we have rather than nothing at all. if tempTimer then tempTimer(3, function() if st.printPending then st.printPending = false icesus.printGuildDetail() end end) end return end icesus.printGuildDetail() end
function icesus.onVitals() local v = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Vitals if not v then return end local s = icesus.state.vitals s.hp = tonumber(v.hp) or s.hp s.sp = tonumber(v.mana) or s.sp s.ep = tonumber(v.moves) or s.ep s.psp = tonumber(v.psp) or s.psp s.hpmax = tonumber(v.maxhp) or s.hpmax s.spmax = tonumber(v.maxmana) or s.spmax s.epmax = tonumber(v.maxmoves) or s.epmax s.pspmax = tonumber(v.maxpsp) or s.pspmax icesus.refreshGauges() -- Guild scalars ride here beside HP. Read from this packet, which -- Mudlet replaces whole, rather than accumulated: a reincarnated -- firepriest must not keep a ghost Fury reading. local scalars = {} for k, val in pairs(v) do if not CORE_VITALS[k] and type(val) == "number" then scalars[k] = val end end icesus.state.guild.scalars = scalars icesus.refreshGuild() end
function icesus.onResources() local r = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Resources local st = icesus.state.guild -- Replaced wholesale, never merged: an empty payload is the server -- saying a block you were shown has gone away. st.resources = (type(r) == "table") and r or {} icesus.refreshGuild() if st.printPending then st.printPending = false icesus.printGuildDetail() end end
function icesus.onMaxstats() local v = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Maxstats if not v then return end local s = icesus.state.vitals s.hpmax = tonumber(v.maxhp) or s.hpmax s.spmax = tonumber(v.maxmana) or s.spmax s.epmax = tonumber(v.maxmoves) or s.epmax s.pspmax = tonumber(v.maxpsp) or s.pspmax icesus.refreshGauges() end
function icesus.onBase() local b = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Base if not b then return end local id = icesus.state.identity if b.name ~= nil then id.name = tostring(b.name) end if b.title ~= nil then id.title = tostring(b.title) end if b.race ~= nil then id.race = tostring(b.race) end if b.guild ~= nil then id.guild = tostring(b.guild) end if b.class ~= nil and (id.guild == nil or id.guild == "") then id.guild = tostring(b.class) -- some servers send 'class' end icesus.refreshIdentity() -- First Char.Base of the session = a character is logged in -- (any creation flow has finished). Everything that would -- otherwise have lit up the character-creation screen with -- banners or mapper chatter is deferred to here. if not icesus.booted then icesus.booted = true if icesus.update.removedGenericMapper then cecho("\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> removed Mudlet's bundled " .. "<yellow>generic_mapper<reset> package " .. "\226\128\148 it conflicts with the Icesus mapper.\n") end cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> v" .. icesus.version .. "<reset> ready. " .. "<grey>Deep, earned progression in a world that rewards commitment.<reset>\n") -- Override files: confirm what loaded, and surface any problem in -- them here rather than on the quiet login screen. pcall(icesus.user.report) -- Tell each profile once that the HUD can be changed at all. A -- player who doesn't know `hud` exists will never read the docs -- that explain it, and a line every session would be nagging. pcall(icesus.hudHint) if icesus.config.autoUpdate and tempTimer then tempTimer(10, function() pcall(icesus.update.check) end) end if icesus.mapper and icesus.mapper.install then icesus.mapper.booted = true icesus.mapper.install() end end end
function icesus.onStatus() local s = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Status if not s then return end
-- identity (level can ride on Status) if s.level ~= nil then icesus.state.identity.level = tonumber(s.level) or 0 icesus.refreshIdentity() end
-- exp / tnl / tna if s.exp ~= nil or s.tnl ~= nil or s.tna ~= nil then icesus.state.exp.exp = tonumber(s.exp) or icesus.state.exp.exp icesus.state.exp.tnl = tonumber(s.tnl) or icesus.state.exp.tnl icesus.state.exp.tna = tonumber(s.tna) or icesus.state.exp.tna icesus.refreshExp() end
-- carry local c = icesus.state.carry if s.money ~= nil then c.money = tonumber(s.money) or 0 end if s.bank ~= nil then c.bank = tonumber(s.bank) or 0 end if s.dfavor ~= nil then c.dfavor = tonumber(s.dfavor) or 0 end if s.carry_wt ~= nil then c.wt = tonumber(s.carry_wt) or 0 end if s.max_wt ~= nil then c.wtmax = tonumber(s.max_wt) or 0 end if s.carry_vol ~= nil then c.vol = tonumber(s.carry_vol) or 0 end if s.max_vol ~= nil then c.volmax = tonumber(s.max_vol) or 0 end if s.money ~= nil or s.dfavor ~= nil or s.carry_wt ~= nil or s.max_wt ~= nil then icesus.refreshCarry() end
-- enemies icesus.state.enemies = {} if type(s.enemies) == "table" and s.enemies[1] then for _, e in ipairs(s.enemies) do table.insert(icesus.state.enemies, { name = e.name or "?", hp = tonumber(e.hp) or 0, shape = e.shape or "", }) end elseif s.enemy and s.enemy ~= "" then table.insert(icesus.state.enemies, { name = s.enemy, hp = tonumber(s.enemypct) or 0, shape = "", }) end icesus.state.inCombat = (s.state == "combat") -- Fighting counts as activity so the mapper holds its save until the -- fight is over (see icesus.mapper.maybeFlush). if icesus.state.inCombat and icesus.mapper and icesus.mapper.touchActivity then icesus.mapper.touchActivity() end icesus.refreshEnemies()
-- momentum icesus.state.momentum = s.momentum or "" icesus.state.specialMomentum = s.special_momentum or "" icesus.state.momentumSource = s.momentum_source or "" icesus.refreshMomentum()
-- effects, and the concealment the player switched on icesus.state.effects = (type(s.effects) == "table") and s.effects or {} icesus.state.stealth = (type(s.stealth) == "table") and s.stealth or {} icesus.state.karmas = (type(s.karmas) == "table") and s.karmas or {} icesus.refreshEffects()
-- Busy state (camping, smelting, fishing, etc.) — a non-spell action -- that blocks input. Char.Casting carries spells; Char.Status.busy -- + activity carries everything else. Both feed the cast bar. if s.busy == 1 or s.busy == true then icesus.state.busy = { activity = tostring(s.activity or "") } else icesus.state.busy = nil end icesus.refreshCasting() end
function icesus.onCasting() local c = gmcp.Char and gmcp.Char.Casting if not c then return end if c.active == 1 or c.active == true then icesus.state.casting = { spell = c.spell or "", progress = tonumber(c.progress) or 0, cps = tonumber(c.cps) or 1, } else icesus.state.casting = nil end icesus.refreshCasting() end
-- Mirror of webclient's exit-list normaliser: Room.Info v2 ships exits -- as a mapping (dir -> destination); v1 ships an array of dirs. Either -- shape collapses into an ordered list of direction names. local DIR_ORDER = { "north", "south", "east", "west", "northeast", "northwest", "southeast", "southwest", "up", "down", "in", "out" } local DIR_SHORT = { north = "n", south = "s", east = "e", west = "w", northeast = "ne", northwest = "nw", southeast = "se", southwest = "sw", up = "u", down = "d", ["in"] = "in", out = "out", }
local function normaliseExits(raw) local out = {} if type(raw) == "table" then -- mapping form: { north = "/some/dest", ... } for _, dir in ipairs(DIR_ORDER) do if raw[dir] ~= nil then table.insert(out, dir) end end -- array form: { "north", "south", ... } — anything not picked above for _, v in ipairs(raw) do if type(v) == "string" then local seen = false for _, d in ipairs(out) do if d == v then seen = true; break end end if not seen then table.insert(out, v) end end end end return out end
function icesus.refreshRoom() if not icesus.hud or not icesus.hud.locationLabel then return end local P = icesus.palette local r = icesus.state.room if (r.name == "" or r.name == nil) and #r.exits == 0 then icesus.hud.locationLabel:echo([[<span style="color:#555">—</span>]]) return end
local left = {} if r.safe then table.insert(left, string.format( [[<span style="color:#5eead4;font-weight:700;font-size:11pt;]] .. [[border:1px solid rgba(94,234,212,0.4);padding:2px 7px;]] .. [[border-radius:3px">SAFE</span>]])) end if r.name ~= "" then table.insert(left, string.format( [[<span style="color:%s;font-weight:600">%s</span>]], P.iceBright, htmlEscape(r.name))) end if r.area ~= "" and r.area ~= "Unknown" then table.insert(left, string.format( [[<span style="color:%s;font-size:13pt">%s</span>]], P.textDim, htmlEscape(r.area))) end
local sep = string.format( [[<span style="color:%s"> · </span>]], P.borderBright)
local exits = {} for _, d in ipairs(r.exits) do table.insert(exits, string.format( [[<span style="color:%s;font-weight:700">%s</span>]], P.ice, DIR_SHORT[d] or htmlEscape(d))) end local exitText = "" if #exits > 0 then exitText = string.format( [[<span style="color:%s">exits:</span> %s]], P.textDim, table.concat(exits, " ")) end
-- HTML table keeps the location flush left and the exits flush right -- in the same row even though Geyser.Label has no flex layout. The -- explicit cellpadding stops "Vaerlonexits:" running together when -- the bigger font shoves the columns up against each other. icesus.hud.locationLabel:echo(string.format( [[<table width="100%%" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="6">]] .. [[<tr><td align="left">%s</td>]] .. [[<td align="right">%s</td></tr></table>]], table.concat(left, sep), exitText)) end
function icesus.onRoomInfo() local r = gmcp.Room and gmcp.Room.Info if not r then return end local s = icesus.state.room if r.name ~= nil then s.name = tostring(r.name) end if r.area ~= nil then s.area = tostring(r.area) end s.exits = normaliseExits(r.exits) s.safe = (r.safe == 1) or (r.safe == true) icesus.refreshRoom() -- Mapper bookkeeping is gated on Char.Base (see onBase). The -- location/exits HUD row above still updates because it has no -- effect outside our own UI; the mapper, on the other hand, -- mutates Mudlet's persistent map data. if icesus.mapper and icesus.mapper.onRoomInfo and icesus.mapper.booted then local ok, err = pcall(icesus.mapper.onRoomInfo, r) if not ok then cecho("\n<red>icesus.mapper error:<reset> " .. tostring(err) .. "\n") end end end
-- ============================================================= -- Mapper — drive Mudlet's built-in mapper from gmcp.Room.Info. -- -- The server ships room.id (8-char hex), exits (dir -> 8-char hash -- of destination, or 0 for shrouded/dynamic), and optionally coords -- for outworld grid rooms. We translate that into Mudlet's integer -- roomID space and call addRoom / setExit / addSpecialExit / -- setRoomCoordinates so the F11 mapper view populates as the -- player walks. Mapper-hostile rooms (server omits id) are -- skipped — they stay invisible to the map. -- -- State persistence: idToRoom (hex -> int) is saved to -- getMudletHomeDir().."/Icesus.idmap.lua" so room numbering is -- stable across reconnects. The map itself is saved via Mudlet's -- saveMap(path) — same lifecycle. -- =============================================================
icesus.mapper = icesus.mapper or {}
local CARDINALS = { north=true, south=true, east=true, west=true, northeast=true, northwest=true, southeast=true, southwest=true, up=true, down=true, ["in"]=true, out=true, }
-- Per-direction offsets in Mudlet's mapper coord system (+y = north, -- the geographic convention where north sits at the top of the map). -- Used for indoor rooms where the server ships no coords — we lay them -- out relative to the room the player just left so the topology shows -- up on screen instead of every room piling on top of (0,0,0). local DIR_OFFSET = { north = { 0, 1, 0 }, south = { 0, -1, 0 }, east = { 1, 0, 0 }, west = {-1, 0, 0 }, northeast = { 1, 1, 0 }, northwest = {-1, 1, 0 }, southeast = { 1, -1, 0 }, southwest = {-1, -1, 0 }, up = { 0, 0, 1 }, down = { 0, 0,-1 }, ["in"] = { 0, 0, 0 }, out = { 0, 0, 0 }, }
-- The bulk-fill terrains — what roads mode exists to NOT map. -- The filter is deliberately inverted (skip these, keep everything -- else) so special tiles survive without us having to enumerate -- them: mine entrances ('?') and province/city buildings ('c', 'O', -- …) ship their own codes, and an unknown code must always mean -- "interesting", never "dropped". -- -- Keep this list in step with gmcp_d.c::send_room_info's terrain -- switch. Every walkable bulk fill the server can name has to appear -- here or roads mode keeps it: badlands (17.3k tiles) and ashlands -- (6.1k) used to fall through the server's switch with no terrain -- field at all, which the rule below reads as "interesting" — that -- was ~3% of the world's land kept by a mode whose whole job is to -- drop it. local BULK_TERRAIN = { water=true, swamp=true, mountain=true, plains=true, forest=true, ice=true, badlands=true, ashlands=true, }
-- Roads-mode verdict for an outworld tile: skip only a recognised -- bulk fill with nothing but plain cardinal exits. Roads, paths, -- unknown codes, missing terrain, and any tile with a special exit -- (it leads somewhere — a gate, an entrance) are all kept. local function outworldBulk(r) local t = r.terrain if t == nil or t == "road" or t == "path" then return false end if not BULK_TERRAIN[t] then return false end if type(r.exits) == "table" then for dir in pairs(r.exits) do if not CARDINALS[dir] then return false end end end return true end
-- Terrain glyph + env mapping. Server ships r.terrain for outworld -- tiles as categorical names (see gmcp_d.c::send_room_info: road, -- path, water, swamp, mountain, plains, forest, ice, badlands, -- ashlands, or the raw map glyph for rarer landmarks). We render -- a glyph in the room cell for distinctive features only (water, -- swamp, mountain) and let env color carry the identity for the -- broader fills (forest, plains, ice). Indoor rooms ship no -- terrain and keep Mudlet's default env. local TERRAIN_CHAR = { road = "#", path = ".", water = "~", swamp = "s", mountain = "^", }
-- Env ids above 16 are safe — Mudlet's built-ins occupy 1-16. RGBs -- mirror the pinkfish "classic" 16-color palette (the pre-2026-04 -- terminal look, see /adm/daemons/outworld_palette_d.c). Registered -- once at mapper.install() via setCustomEnvColor. local TERRAIN_ENV = { road = 200, -- YELLOW (brown) path = 201, -- WHITE (worn track) water = 202, -- BLUE swamp = 203, -- RED mountain = 204, -- HI_BLACK (gray) plains = 205, -- HI_YELLOW forest = 206, -- GREEN ice = 207, -- HI_CYAN badlands = 209, -- MAGENTA -- 'a' is WHITE in the classic palette, which is already the worn -- track's colour — silver from the current palette instead, so ash -- flats and paths don't read as the same tile. ashlands = 210, -- SILVER }
-- Fully transparent env for the position-cursor room: the cell draws -- nothing at all — Mudlet's own player marker is the only indicator. local CURSOR_ENV = 208
local function setupTerrainEnvs() if not setCustomEnvColor then return end pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.road, 170, 85, 0, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.path, 170, 170, 170, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.water, 0, 0, 170, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.swamp, 170, 0, 0, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.mountain, 85, 85, 85, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.plains, 255, 255, 85, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.forest, 0, 170, 0, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.ice, 85, 255, 255, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.badlands, 170, 0, 170, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, TERRAIN_ENV.ashlands, 192, 192, 192, 255) pcall(setCustomEnvColor, CURSOR_ENV, 0, 0, 0, 0) end
local function mapDataPath() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/Icesus.map.dat" end local function idMapPath() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/Icesus.idmap.lua" end local function backupDir() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/Icesus.backup" end -- Written just before loadMap, removed once the loaded map answers a -- probe. Still on disk at boot = the previous session died inside -- that window (loadMap segfaults on a truncated .dat and pcall can't -- catch C++ crashes) — see icesus.mapper.install. local function sentinelPath() return getMudletHomeDir() .. "/Icesus.map.loading" end
-- Plain binary copy — Mudlet's Lua has no io.copy and the map .dat -- is binary ("rb"/"wb" keeps Windows from mangling it). local function copyFile(src, dst) local fin = io.open(src, "rb") if not fin then return false end local data = fin:read("*a") fin:close() if not data then return false end local fout = io.open(dst, "wb") if not fout then return false end fout:write(data) fout:close() return true end
-- Overwrite-rename. POSIX os.rename replaces the target atomically; -- Windows refuses, so fall back to remove-then-rename. Dying inside -- that tiny window leaves the validated source file on disk, which -- still beats a half-written target. local function promote(src, dst) if os.rename(src, dst) then return true end os.remove(dst) return os.rename(src, dst) and true or false end
local function loadIdMap() local t = {} if io.exists and io.exists(idMapPath()) then local ok = pcall(table.load, idMapPath(), t) if not ok or type(t.idToRoom) ~= "table" then -- The file exists but doesn't parse (truncated write, disk -- glitch). Every file saveIdMap ever writes contains idToRoom, -- so a miss here is corruption, not age. Starting silently from -- scratch would double every room on the map — say so, and -- point at the backups. t = {} cecho("\n<red>Icesus<reset> mapper: Icesus.idmap.lua is unreadable " .. "\226\128\148 room identity data lost. <yellow>mapper " .. "restore<reset> lists backups you can roll back to.\n") end end t.idToRoom = t.idToRoom or {} t.areaToInt = t.areaToInt or {} t.placed = t.placed or {} t.gridmoded = t.gridmoded or {} -- areaId -> true once gridmode is on t.areaCoords = t.areaCoords or {} -- areaId -> { "x,y,z" -> true } occupancy t.seen = t.seen or {} -- hexId -> Room.Info signature (walk fast-path) -- next_id starts above any in-use Mudlet room. createRoomID() -- gives us the next free int the engine knows about; we take -- the max of that and our saved counter so a wiped idmap with -- existing map data doesn't collide. local engineNext = 1 if createRoomID then local ok, v = pcall(createRoomID); if ok and type(v) == "number" then engineNext = v end end t.next_id = math.max(t.next_id or 1, engineNext) return t end
local function markCoord(areaId, x, y, z) if not areaId or areaId <= 0 then return end local m = icesus.mapper.idMap -- areaCoords + gridmoded were introduced in v1.0.10. On a hot -- upgrade from an older build, icesus.mapper.idMap survives in -- memory without these fields — initialise lazily here so we -- don't index nil. m.areaCoords = m.areaCoords or {} m.areaCoords[areaId] = m.areaCoords[areaId] or {} m.areaCoords[areaId][x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z] = true end
-- Find an unused (x, y, z) in this area, starting at the requested -- coordinate and spiralling outward on the z-plane. Used to scatter -- indoor buildings (Shanty Town, inn cellars, …) near their entrance -- tiles instead of piling them all at (0,0,0). -- Is a cell still free in this area's occupancy map? local function coordFree(areaId, x, y, z) if not areaId or areaId <= 0 then return true end local m = icesus.mapper.idMap local used = m.areaCoords and m.areaCoords[areaId] if not used then return true end return not used[x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z] end
local function freeCoord(areaId, baseX, baseY, baseZ) local m = icesus.mapper.idMap m.areaCoords = m.areaCoords or {} -- see markCoord note m.areaCoords[areaId] = m.areaCoords[areaId] or {} local used = m.areaCoords[areaId] local function key(x, y, z) return x .. "," .. y .. "," .. z end if not used[key(baseX, baseY, baseZ)] then used[key(baseX, baseY, baseZ)] = true return baseX, baseY, baseZ end for radius = 1, 50 do for dx = -radius, radius do for dy = -radius, radius do if math.abs(dx) == radius or math.abs(dy) == radius then local x, y = baseX + dx, baseY + dy local k = key(x, y, baseZ) if not used[k] then used[k] = true return x, y, baseZ end end end end end -- 50-radius search is enough for any sane area; if we get here the -- area is genuinely packed and a collision is better than infinite -- looping. return baseX, baseY, baseZ end
-- Write the idmap atomically: serialise to a sidecar, prove the -- sidecar parses, then rename it over the live file. A crash -- mid-write can only ever cost the sidecar — the live file is always -- a complete, loadable snapshot. local function saveIdMap() local tmp = idMapPath() .. ".new" if not pcall(table.save, tmp, icesus.mapper.idMap) then pcall(os.remove, tmp) return false end local check = {} if not pcall(table.load, tmp, check) or type(check.idToRoom) ~= "table" then pcall(os.remove, tmp) return false end return promote(tmp, idMapPath()) end
-- saveMap counterpart of saveIdMap: write to a sidecar, sanity-check -- it, rename into place. saveMap runs in Mudlet C++ and a shutdown -- racing it is exactly how a truncated .dat ends up crashing the next -- session's loadMap. No Lua-side parser exists for the binary format, -- so the check is call-succeeded + non-empty file. local function saveMapAtomic() if not saveMap then return false end local tmp = mapDataPath() .. ".new" local ok, saved = pcall(saveMap, tmp) if not ok or saved == false then pcall(os.remove, tmp) return false end local f = io.open(tmp, "rb") local size = f and f:seek("end") or 0 if f then f:close() end if size == 0 then pcall(os.remove, tmp) return false end return promote(tmp, mapDataPath()) end
-- ============================================================= -- Backups — a successful flush may snapshot map + idmap as a PAIR -- into Icesus.backup/. The two files only make sense together: -- Mudlet's own map backups can't recover anything because nothing -- backs up the idmap that names those rooms. Generations are spaced -- >= BACKUP_SPACING_SECS apart (sessions run long; snapshotting -- every idle flush would rotate the whole history away in minutes), -- except the first flush of a session and an explicit `mapper save`, -- which always snapshot. -- ============================================================= local BACKUP_KEEP = 5 -- most-recent pairs, whatever their age local BACKUP_DAILY_DAYS = 7 -- plus the first pair of each of these days local BACKUP_SPACING_SECS = 3600
-- Backup pairs on disk, oldest first. Pair = same stamp on both -- files; a half-pair (interrupted copy) is ignored. local function listBackups() local out = {} if not (lfs and lfs.dir and io.exists) then return out end if lfs.attributes(backupDir(), "mode") ~= "directory" then return out end local ok, iter, obj = pcall(lfs.dir, backupDir()) if not ok then return out end for f in iter, obj do local stamp = f:match("^(%d+%-%d+)%.map%.dat$") if stamp and io.exists(backupDir() .. "/" .. stamp .. ".idmap.lua") then out[#out + 1] = stamp end end table.sort(out) return out end
local function makeBackup(force) if not (io.exists and io.exists(mapDataPath()) and io.exists(idMapPath())) then return end local now = os.time() if not force and icesus.mapper.lastBackup and now - icesus.mapper.lastBackup < BACKUP_SPACING_SECS then return end if lfs and lfs.mkdir then pcall(lfs.mkdir, backupDir()) end local base = backupDir() .. "/" .. os.date("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") if copyFile(mapDataPath(), base .. ".map.dat") and copyFile(idMapPath(), base .. ".idmap.lua") then icesus.mapper.lastBackup = now -- Tiered retention. A busy session (session-start backup + a few -- explicit saves) can burn through a recent-N quota in under an -- hour and rotate away the last backup that predates a problem — -- exactly when it's needed most. So beyond the BACKUP_KEEP most -- recent pairs, the FIRST pair of each of the last -- BACKUP_DAILY_DAYS days is protected too: however hectic today -- gets, yesterday's opening state survives. local stamps = listBackups() local protect = {} for i = math.max(1, #stamps - BACKUP_KEEP + 1), #stamps do protect[stamps[i]] = true end local firstOfDay, days = {}, {} for _, s in ipairs(stamps) do local day = s:match("^(%d+)%-") if day and not firstOfDay[day] then firstOfDay[day] = s days[#days + 1] = day end end table.sort(days) for i = math.max(1, #days - BACKUP_DAILY_DAYS + 1), #days do protect[firstOfDay[days[i]]] = true end for _, s in ipairs(stamps) do if not protect[s] then pcall(os.remove, backupDir() .. "/" .. s .. ".map.dat") pcall(os.remove, backupDir() .. "/" .. s .. ".idmap.lua") end end else -- a half-written pair is worse than none pcall(os.remove, base .. ".map.dat") pcall(os.remove, base .. ".idmap.lua") end end
-- Copy a backup pair over the live files. Callers reload afterwards. local function restoreBackupPair(stamp) local base = backupDir() .. "/" .. stamp if not (io.exists and io.exists(base .. ".map.dat") and io.exists(base .. ".idmap.lua")) then return false end return copyFile(base .. ".map.dat", mapDataPath()) and copyFile(base .. ".idmap.lua", idMapPath()) end
-- Move the live pair out of the way, kept as .bad-<stamp> for -- post-mortem instead of deleted. local function quarantineLivePair() local stamp = os.date("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") for _, p in ipairs({ mapDataPath(), idMapPath() }) do if io.exists and io.exists(p) then pcall(promote, p, p .. ".bad-" .. stamp) end end end
local function fmtStamp(stamp) local y, mo, d, h, mi = stamp:match("^(%d%d%d%d)(%d%d)(%d%d)%-(%d%d)(%d%d)") if not y then return stamp end return string.format("%s-%s-%s %s:%s", y, mo, d, h, mi) end
-- True when the engine already carries our rooms. Mudlet auto-loads -- the profile's own copy of the map before any script runs, and -- calling loadMap() on top of a populated map makes the engine tear -- down and rebuild every room one at a time — on a 10k-room map -- that's minutes of frozen UI at login, which reads exactly like -- "Mudlet crashes when I connect" (and got players deleting their -- map files to get back in). Sample a few idmap entries; any hit -- means the map in the engine is ours. -- -- Identity only. "Ours" does not mean "current" — see engineCoverage. local function mapAlreadyLive(m) if not (m and roomExists) then return false end local sampled, present = 0, 0 for _, rid in pairs(m.idToRoom or {}) do sampled = sampled + 1 local ok, hit = pcall(roomExists, rid) if ok and hit then present = present + 1 end if sampled >= 5 then break end end return present > 0 end
-- How much of the idmap has to be live before we accept the map the -- engine already holds as the same generation as Icesus.map.dat. Not -- 1.0: a room deleted in Mudlet's map editor (issue #7) is normal and -- must not force a full reload at every login. local MAP_FRESH_RATIO = 0.95
-- How many of the idmap's rooms the engine actually holds. -- mapAlreadyLive's 5-room sample answers "is this our map?"; this -- answers "is it the map our idmap was saved with?" — a different -- question, because Mudlet writes its own copy of the map on its own -- schedule (profile close) while the package saves to an explicit -- path that never touches that copy. Kill Mudlet and the two fall out -- of step: the auto-loaded map can be sessions behind the .dat, and -- accepting it silently drops every room mapped since, then writes -- the shortfall back over the good file on the next flush. -- -- One pass over the idmap, one roomExists each — a few ms on a 12k -- map, once per login. local function engineCoverage(m) if not (m and roomExists) then return 0, 0 end local known, live = 0, 0 local ok = pcall(function() for _, rid in pairs(m.idToRoom or {}) do known = known + 1 if roomExists(rid) then live = live + 1 end end end) if not ok then return 0, 0 end return known, live end
-- Resolve a server hex_id to a Mudlet integer roomID, creating the -- room with addRoom() the first time we see it. Pre-creating -- destination rooms before the player walks there lets Mudlet's -- auto-layout draw stubbed neighbours instead of empty space. local function ensureRoom(hexId) local m = icesus.mapper.idMap local roomId = m.idToRoom[hexId] if roomId then if not roomExists or roomExists(roomId) then return roomId end -- The player deleted this room in Mudlet's map editor (issue #7). -- Trusting the cached id would aim every set* call at a room that -- isn't there — silent no-ops, and the room never comes back. -- Re-add it under the same integer id and forget its placement -- and signature so the next Room.Info rebuilds it in full. if addRoom and addRoom(roomId) ~= false then m.placed[hexId] = nil if m.seen then m.seen[hexId] = nil end icesus.mapper.dirty = true return roomId, true end -- Couldn't reclaim the old id — mint a fresh one below. m.idToRoom[hexId] = nil m.placed[hexId] = nil if m.seen then m.seen[hexId] = nil end end local id = m.next_id m.next_id = id + 1 local ok = addRoom and addRoom(id) if ok == false then -- collision (engine already used this int) — bump and retry repeat id = m.next_id m.next_id = id + 1 ok = addRoom and addRoom(id) until ok ~= false end m.idToRoom[hexId] = id icesus.mapper.dirty = true return id, true end
local function ensureArea(name) if not name or name == "" then return -1 end local m = icesus.mapper.idMap local areaId = m.areaToInt[name] if areaId then return areaId end
-- Areas outlive both our rooms and our id table. deleteRoom leaves -- the area behind, so `mapper reset`, the v1.0.16 idmap quarantine, -- and "player deleted Icesus.idmap.lua but kept the map" all end up -- with Mudlet holding every area name while areaToInt is empty. In -- that state addAreaName refuses the name and returns -1, which used -- to mean every room landed in Default Area and the outworld never -- got gridmode (issue #12). Adopt the existing area instead. if getAreaTable then local ok, tbl = pcall(getAreaTable) if ok and type(tbl) == "table" then local existing = tonumber(tbl[name]) if existing and existing > 0 then m.areaToInt[name] = existing icesus.mapper.dirty = true return existing end end end
local ok, v = pcall(addAreaName, name) if ok and type(v) == "number" and v > 0 then areaId = v m.areaToInt[name] = areaId icesus.mapper.dirty = true end return areaId or -1 end
-- "You are here" cursor for outworld tiles the mapping mode skips. -- One reusable room, kept out of idToRoom, moved to the player's -- grid coordinates and centered — so the map keeps tracking the ride -- across unmapped terrain instead of freezing on the last real room. local function moveCursor(m, r) if not addRoom or type(r.coords) ~= "table" then return end local x = tonumber(r.coords[1]) local y = tonumber(r.coords[2]) local z = tonumber(r.coords[3] or 0) or 0 if not (x and y) then return end local cur = m.cursorRoom if not (cur and (not roomExists or roomExists(cur))) then cur = nil for _ = 1, 32 do local id = m.next_id m.next_id = id + 1 if addRoom(id) ~= false then cur = id; break end end if not cur then return end m.cursorRoom = cur icesus.mapper.noteDirty() -- persist cursorRoom so it's reused end -- Invisible on purpose: Mudlet already draws its own player marker -- on the centered room, so the cursor cell itself must not add -- anything to the map. Restyled once per session (not just at -- creation) so a cursor inherited from an older build loses its -- '@' glyph too. if not icesus.mapper.cursorStyled then icesus.mapper.cursorStyled = true if setRoomEnv then pcall(setRoomEnv, cur, CURSOR_ENV) end if setRoomChar then pcall(setRoomChar, cur, "") end end if r.area and r.area ~= "" then local areaId = ensureArea(tostring(r.area)) if areaId and areaId > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, cur, areaId) end end if r.name then pcall(setRoomName, cur, tostring(r.name)) end pcall(setRoomCoordinates, cur, x, -y, z) if centerview then pcall(centerview, cur) end end
-- Signature of everything onRoomInfo consumes from a Room.Info -- payload (name, area, sorted exits, coords, terrain). Lets us tell -- "walked back into a room we already mapped, unchanged" apart from -- "something about this room actually moved" without touching the map. -- Approach contributed by Steve De Jongh (sdejongh / Arthr), PR #5. local function roomSig(r) local p = { tostring(r.name or ""), tostring(r.area or "") } if type(r.exits) == "table" then local k = {} for dir, dest in pairs(r.exits) do k[#k+1] = tostring(dir) .. "=" .. tostring(dest) end table.sort(k) p[#p+1] = table.concat(k, ",") end if type(r.coords) == "table" then p[#p+1] = table.concat(r.coords, ",") end if type(r.terrain) == "string" then p[#p+1] = r.terrain end return table.concat(p, "|") end
function icesus.mapper.onRoomInfo(r) if not addRoom or not setExit then return end -- pre-mapper build if icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapperEnabled == false then return -- paused via `mapper off` end if type(r) ~= "table" then return end local hexId = r.id if type(hexId) ~= "string" or hexId == "" then return end if not icesus.mapper.idMap then icesus.mapper.idMap = loadIdMap() end local m = icesus.mapper.idMap icesus.mapper.touchActivity() -- walking = activity, defers the save
-- Outworld thinning (`mapper outworld roads|off`). Tiles mapped -- before a mode switch stay useful — recenter on them, add nothing; -- unmapped tiles are ignored entirely. Indoor zones (no coords) are -- never affected. local isOutworld = type(r.coords) == "table" and #r.coords >= 2 local owMode = (icesus.settings and icesus.settings.outworldMode) or "full" local roadsOnly = isOutworld and owMode == "roads" if isOutworld and owMode ~= "full" then if owMode == "off" or (roadsOnly and outworldBulk(r)) then local known = m.idToRoom[hexId] local live = known and (not roomExists or roomExists(known)) if live and roadsOnly then -- Roads mode prunes ONLY Default Area strays — the ghost -- rooms pre-created before area inheritance existed. Bulk -- tiles properly mapped back in full mode keep their room: -- the player chose to keep that map, we just stop growing -- it. When pruning, center the cursor FIRST so the -- player-room pointer never dangles on the deleted room -- (the centerview segfault documented at reset()). local aid = nil if getRoomArea then local okA, v = pcall(getRoomArea, known) if okA then aid = v end end if aid ~= nil and aid <= 0 then icesus.mapper.lastHexId = nil moveCursor(m, r) if deleteRoom then pcall(deleteRoom, known) end m.idToRoom[hexId] = nil m.placed[hexId] = nil if m.seen then m.seen[hexId] = nil end icesus.mapper.noteDirty() else if centerview then pcall(centerview, known) end icesus.mapper.lastHexId = hexId end elseif live then -- off mode: the map is frozen — nothing is added or removed. -- Repair strays before centering: a room pre-created before -- area inheritance existed may still sit in Default Area, -- and centerview on it flips the whole mapper view there. if r.area and r.area ~= "" and getRoomArea then local okA, aid = pcall(getRoomArea, known) if okA and (not aid or aid <= 0) then local realArea = ensureArea(tostring(r.area)) if realArea and realArea > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, known, realArea) icesus.mapper.noteDirty() end end end if centerview then pcall(centerview, known) end icesus.mapper.lastHexId = hexId else icesus.mapper.lastHexId = nil -- don't anchor buildings to a ghost moveCursor(m, r) -- keep the view on the player end return end end
-- Fast path: a room whose signature is unchanged since we last -- processed it needs no map writes at all — every set* call below -- would re-apply identical data, but each one still marks the map -- dirty, which drags saveMap + table.save behind every step and -- shows up as walking latency (issue #4). Just recenter and leave -- the dirty flag alone so flushSave stays a no-op too. The cache -- lives in idMap, so it persists across sessions and is wiped with -- the rest of the state on mapper reset / stale-map detection. m.seen = m.seen or {} -- hot-upgrade safety (pre-v1.0.14 idMap) local sig = roomSig(r) if m.seen[hexId] == sig then local known = m.idToRoom[hexId] if known and (not roomExists or roomExists(known)) then if centerview then pcall(centerview, known) end icesus.mapper.lastHexId = hexId return end -- Signature unchanged but the Mudlet room is gone — deleted in -- the map editor (issue #7). Deleting it also severed each -- neighbour's exit into it, and the neighbours' own signatures -- still match, so they would fast-path forever with the link -- missing. Forget their signatures too: the next visit rebuilds -- them and rewires the way back in. Then fall through so -- ensureRoom re-adds this room itself. if type(r.exits) == "table" then for _, dest in pairs(r.exits) do if type(dest) == "string" and dest ~= "" and dest ~= "0" then m.seen[dest] = nil end end end end
local roomId, createdNow = ensureRoom(hexId)
-- A room the neighbours couldn't link to before now exists — forget -- their signatures so their next visit rebuilds and wires the way -- in. Only the neighbour's own Room.Info can say which way that is: -- the outworld grid is NOT reliably symmetric, so an exit here does -- not license writing the reverse one over there (rivers carry you -- in without letting you back out; ~2.7% of sampled outworld links -- are one-way). Costs one rebuild pass per direction, after which -- the fast path goes quiet for good. if createdNow and type(r.exits) == "table" and m.seen then for dir, dest in pairs(r.exits) do if type(dest) == "string" then m.seen[dest] = nil end end end
-- Room name + area. Update unconditionally: rare renames + area -- changes both need to propagate. if r.name then pcall(setRoomName, roomId, tostring(r.name)) end local areaId = -1 if r.area and r.area ~= "" then areaId = ensureArea(tostring(r.area)) if areaId and areaId > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, roomId, areaId) end end
-- Coords. Outworld grid rooms get absolute server coords with Y -- flipped: the server's y grows southward (top-down array index), -- Mudlet's grows northward (geographic convention). Indoor rooms -- ship no coords — we anchor each new building near the room the -- player just stepped out of (lastHexId) and let freeCoord pick a -- collision-free spot so multiple buildings in the same area -- don't pile up at the origin. if type(r.coords) == "table" and #r.coords >= 2 then local x = tonumber(r.coords[1]) local y = tonumber(r.coords[2]) local z = tonumber(r.coords[3] or 0) or 0 if x and y then pcall(setRoomCoordinates, roomId, x, -y, z) m.placed[hexId] = { x, -y, z } markCoord(areaId, x, -y, z) -- r.coords is the server's signal that this tile is outworld. -- Flip the area to gridmode the first time we see it — the -- map reads as a pixel map instead of node-and-line graph. m.gridmoded = m.gridmoded or {} -- hot-upgrade safety if areaId > 0 and not m.gridmoded[areaId] and setGridMode then m.gridmoded[areaId] = true pcall(setGridMode, areaId, true) icesus.mapper.dirty = true end end end if not m.placed[hexId] then -- Anchor unplaced indoor rooms near the last room we saw -- (typically where the player just walked from), then scan -- outward for a free slot per-area. local baseX, baseY, baseZ = 0, 0, 0 local last = icesus.mapper.lastHexId if last and m.placed[last] then local p = m.placed[last] baseX, baseY, baseZ = p[1], p[2], p[3] end local fx, fy, fz = freeCoord(areaId, baseX, baseY, baseZ) pcall(setRoomCoordinates, roomId, fx, fy, fz) m.placed[hexId] = { fx, fy, fz } elseif areaId and areaId > 0 then -- Already placed, usually by a neighbour's pre-placement guess, -- which could only register the cell under *that* room's area. Now -- that the room has told us which area it is actually in, claim the -- cell there too, or freeCoord will hand it to the next building. local p = m.placed[hexId] markCoord(areaId, p[1], p[2], p[3]) end
-- Terrain glyph + env tint. Server ships r.terrain for every tile -- on the main world map; indoor rooms and the six planes (which -- have their own maps the server does not read here) ship none and -- keep Mudlet's default rendering. if type(r.terrain) == "string" then local tc = TERRAIN_CHAR[r.terrain] if not tc and #r.terrain <= 2 and not TERRAIN_ENV[r.terrain] then -- Unknown short code ('?' mine entrances, 'c'/'O' province and -- city buildings, legacy single-char terrains): render it as-is, -- like the game's own -- overhead map does. The length guard keeps full words like -- "plains" from being painted into a room cell. tc = r.terrain end if tc and setRoomChar then pcall(setRoomChar, roomId, tc) end local te = TERRAIN_ENV[r.terrain] if te and setRoomEnv then pcall(setRoomEnv, roomId, te) end end
-- Exits. The server sends a mapping dir -> dest_hash. dest_hash -- of 0 means shrouded / unknown destination (still plot the -- direction stub so the player sees the option). Cardinal exits -- go through setExit, anything else (e.g. "enter shop") through -- addSpecialExit. local exits = r.exits if type(exits) == "table" then -- Track what's still live so we can prune disappeared exits. local liveCardinals = {} local liveSpecials = {} for dir, dest in pairs(exits) do if type(dir) == "string" and dir ~= "" then local destHash if type(dest) == "string" and dest ~= "" and dest ~= "0" then destHash = dest end if CARDINALS[dir] then liveCardinals[dir] = true -- Roads mode: don't pre-create unmapped outworld -- neighbours — that 8-per-tile fan-out is what balloons -- the outworld area. Link tiles already on the map, stub -- the rest. local linkable = destHash and (not roadsOnly or m.idToRoom[destHash]) if linkable then local destId, destNew = ensureRoom(destHash) pcall(setExit, roomId, destId, dir) -- Outworld only: give a freshly pre-created tile the -- current area right away (its own visit corrects it if -- it's actually across a border). Without this, the whole -- unvisited frontier collects in Mudlet's "Default Area" -- as a ghost outline of the explored map. Indoor zones -- keep the historical behaviour — unvisited neighbours -- stay out of the drawn area until actually entered. if destNew and isOutworld and areaId and areaId > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, destId, areaId) end -- Position unplaced destinations relative to this room so -- Mudlet draws a graph instead of stacking everything at -- the origin. Once a room has coords (here or via server -- r.coords), they stay sticky — we don't reshuffle. if not m.placed[destHash] and m.placed[hexId] and DIR_OFFSET[dir] then local p = m.placed[hexId] local o = DIR_OFFSET[dir] local dx, dy, dz = p[1] + o[1], p[2] + o[2], p[3] + o[3] -- Offsetting from this room is a guess about a room we -- have never been in, and indoor layouts are not grids: -- two rooms can both guess the same cell and land on top -- of each other (issue #12, "a lot of overlap"). Take the -- guess only while the cell is free; otherwise leave the -- room unplaced and let its own Room.Info place it, by -- server coords outworld or freeCoord indoors. if coordFree(areaId, dx, dy, dz) then pcall(setRoomCoordinates, destId, dx, dy, dz) m.placed[destHash] = { dx, dy, dz } -- Same-area cardinal neighbour — register the slot so -- freeCoord (for future buildings) knows it's taken. markCoord(areaId, dx, dy, dz) end end elseif setExitStub then -- Cardinal exit with unknown destination — stub so the -- direction renders, but don't draw a line. pcall(setExit, roomId, -1, dir) -- clear any prior link pcall(setExitStub, roomId, dir, true) end else liveSpecials[dir] = true if destHash and (not roadsOnly or m.idToRoom[destHash]) then local destId, destNew = ensureRoom(destHash) pcall(addSpecialExit, roomId, destId, dir) if destNew and isOutworld and areaId and areaId > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, destId, areaId) end end -- Special exits with unknown destinations can't be -- represented in Mudlet without a real target — skip. end end end -- Prune cardinal exits that are no longer present. if getRoomExits then local ok, existing = pcall(getRoomExits, roomId) if ok and type(existing) == "table" then for dir in pairs(existing) do if not liveCardinals[dir] then pcall(setExit, roomId, -1, dir) end end end end -- Prune special exits we placed earlier that are now gone. -- getSpecialExitsSwap, not getSpecialExits: the latter is keyed by -- destination room id, with the commands in a table underneath, so -- comparing its keys against command names never matched and every -- rebuild cleared and re-added the lot. The swap variant is the one -- keyed by command, which is what liveSpecials holds. if clearSpecialExits and getSpecialExitsSwap then local ok, existing = pcall(getSpecialExitsSwap, roomId) if ok and type(existing) == "table" then local needRebuild = false for cmd in pairs(existing) do if not liveSpecials[cmd] then needRebuild = true; break end end if needRebuild then pcall(clearSpecialExits, roomId) for cmd in pairs(liveSpecials) do local destHash = exits[cmd] if destHash and destHash ~= "0" and (not roadsOnly or m.idToRoom[destHash]) then local destId, destNew = ensureRoom(destHash) pcall(addSpecialExit, roomId, destId, cmd) if destNew and isOutworld and areaId and areaId > 0 then pcall(setRoomArea, destId, areaId) end end end end end end end
if centerview then pcall(centerview, roomId) end icesus.mapper.lastHexId = hexId -- anchor next indoor room here m.seen[hexId] = sig -- full rebuild done — arm the fast path icesus.mapper.noteDirty() end
function icesus.mapper.flushSave(forceBackup) if not icesus.mapper.dirty then return end local m = icesus.mapper.idMap if m and next(m.idToRoom or {}) and not mapAlreadyLive(m) then -- The idmap says we've mapped rooms, but none of the sampled ones -- exist in the engine: the in-memory map has been wiped out from -- under us (a load that came out empty, an external delete). -- Saving now would overwrite the good snapshot on disk with an -- empty shell — the exact way players actually lost their maps. -- Refuse, and say so once instead of once per poll. if not icesus.mapper.wipeWarned then icesus.mapper.wipeWarned = true cecho("\n<red>Icesus<reset> map save blocked \226\128\148 the " .. "in-memory map looks wiped (mapped rooms missing from " .. "Mudlet). Saving would overwrite your good map file with an " .. "empty one. Restart the profile, or roll back with " .. "<yellow>mapper restore<reset>; <yellow>mapper reset<reset> " .. "if you really want to start over.\n") end return end icesus.mapper.wipeWarned = nil local mapOk = saveMapAtomic() local idOk = saveIdMap() if not (mapOk and idOk) then -- Failed write (disk full, locked file): keep the dirty flag so -- the idle poll retries and the HUD badge keeps telling the -- truth. The live files still hold the previous good snapshot — -- that's the point of the sidecar-then-rename dance. return end makeBackup(forceBackup) icesus.mapper.dirty = false icesus.mapper.dirtyCount = 0 icesus.mapper.dirtySince = nil icesus.mapper.lastSave = os.time() icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() end
-- Record one unsaved map change and surface it on the HUD badge. -- Called once per full onRoomInfo rebuild (the walk fast-path never -- gets here), so the badge counter reads as "rooms mapped since the -- last save". function icesus.mapper.noteDirty() icesus.mapper.dirty = true icesus.mapper.dirtyCount = (icesus.mapper.dirtyCount or 0) + 1 icesus.mapper.dirtySince = icesus.mapper.dirtySince or os.time() icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() end
-- Keep the location-row save controls in sync: the badge shows pending -- unsaved changes (click = flush now), the pill shows the save mode -- (click = toggle auto/manual). function icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() if not icesus.hud then return end local badge = icesus.hud.mapSaveBadge local pill = icesus.hud.mapModeBtn if badge then if icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapperEnabled == false then badge:echo( [[<center><span style="color:#f87171;font-weight:700">map: off</span></center>]]) elseif icesus.mapper.dirty then badge:echo(string.format( [[<center><span style="color:#fbbf24;font-weight:700">map: %d unsaved</span></center>]], icesus.mapper.dirtyCount or 0)) else badge:echo([[<center><span style="color:#555">map saved</span></center>]]) end end if pill then local mode = (icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapSaveMode) or "auto" pill:echo(string.format( [[<center><span style="color:%s">save: <b>%s</b></span></center>]], mode == "manual" and "#7dd3fc" or "#8b90a5", mode)) end end
-- `mapper save` / badge click — flush now, with feedback. function icesus.mapper.saveCommand() if not icesus.mapper.dirty then -- Nothing to flush, but an explicit save is a request for a -- restore point — snapshot the current pair regardless of the -- hourly spacing. makeBackup(true) cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map already saved (backup refreshed).\n") return end local n = icesus.mapper.dirtyCount or 0 icesus.mapper.flushSave(true) if icesus.mapper.dirty then cecho("\n<red>Icesus<reset> map save failed \226\128\148 the previous " .. "snapshot on disk is untouched; check disk space and retry.\n") return end cecho(string.format( "\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map saved (%d change%s flushed).\n", n, n == 1 and "" or "s")) end
-- `mapper restore` — list backup pairs; `mapper restore <n>` — roll -- the live map + idmap back to pair n (1 = most recent). The current -- pair is quarantined as .bad-<stamp> first, so a restore is never -- destructive. function icesus.mapper.restoreCommand(arg) local stamps = listBackups() if #stamps == 0 then cecho("\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> no map backups yet \226\128\148 one is " .. "taken on the first save of each session, then hourly, and on " .. "every explicit <yellow>mapper save<reset>.\n") return end local ordered = {} for i = #stamps, 1, -1 do ordered[#ordered + 1] = stamps[i] end if not arg or arg == "" then cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map backups " .. "(<yellow>mapper restore N<reset> to roll back):\n") for i, stamp in ipairs(ordered) do cecho(string.format(" <yellow>%d<reset> %s\n", i, fmtStamp(stamp))) end return end local n = tonumber(arg) local stamp = n and ordered[n] if not stamp then cecho(string.format( "\n<red>Icesus<reset> no backup #%s \226\128\148 <yellow>mapper " .. "restore<reset> lists the %d available.\n", tostring(arg), #ordered)) return end quarantineLivePair() if not restoreBackupPair(stamp) then cecho("\n<red>Icesus<reset> restore failed \226\128\148 backup pair " .. "unreadable. The current map was set aside as .bad-* files in " .. "the profile folder.\n") return end -- Reload the restored pair in place of the in-memory state. Warn -- first: on a big map the rebuild takes a while and a force-quit -- halfway through is how load problems turn into data loss. cecho("\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> restoring \226\128\148 rebuilding the " .. "in-memory map. Mudlet may freeze for a bit on a large map; " .. "let it finish.\n") -- Empty the engine of the current rooms before loading the backup. -- Restoring straight over a populated map makes every room in the -- .dat collide with a live one; the engine burns minutes tearing -- each collision down and (on some builds) comes out the other side -- with a broken, empty map. Deleting through our own idToRoom first -- (same approach as reset()) hands loadMap an empty room DB — the -- fast path, and the one that actually works. local old = icesus.mapper.idMap if old and deleteRoom then for _, rid in pairs(old.idToRoom or {}) do pcall(deleteRoom, rid) end if old.cursorRoom then pcall(deleteRoom, old.cursorRoom) end end icesus.mapper.idMap = nil if loadMap and io.exists and io.exists(mapDataPath()) then pcall(loadMap, mapDataPath()) end icesus.mapper.idMap = loadIdMap() icesus.mapper.lastHexId = nil icesus.mapper.dirty = false icesus.mapper.dirtyCount = 0 icesus.mapper.dirtySince = nil if updateMap then pcall(updateMap) end icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() cecho(string.format( "\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map restored from backup %s. The map " .. "you replaced is kept as .bad-* files. Take a step to re-sync.\n", fmtStamp(stamp))) end
function icesus.mapper.setSaveMode(mode) mode = (mode == "manual") and "manual" or "auto" icesus.settings = icesus.settings or {} icesus.settings.mapSaveMode = mode icesus.saveSettings() icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() if mode == "auto" then cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map autosave <lime_green>on<reset> " .. "\226\128\148 the map is flushed in quiet moments.\n") else cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map autosave <yellow>off<reset> " .. "\226\128\148 save with <yellow>mapper save<reset> or the HUD " .. "badge; the map is still saved on exit and disconnect.\n") end end
function icesus.mapper.toggleSaveMode() local cur = (icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapSaveMode) or "auto" icesus.mapper.setSaveMode(cur == "auto" and "manual" or "auto") end
-- `mapper on|off` — pause / resume the mapper entirely. Off freezes -- the map exactly as it is: Room.Info packets are ignored, so nothing -- is added, rewired or recentered, and the saved files stay put. The -- kill switch when the mapper misbehaves mid-session and the player -- doesn't want a destructive `mapper reset`. Persisted across -- sessions; state shows as "map: off" on the HUD badge. function icesus.mapper.setEnabled(on) icesus.settings = icesus.settings or {} icesus.settings.mapperEnabled = on and true or false icesus.saveSettings() icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI() if on then cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> mapper <lime_green>on<reset> " .. "\226\128\148 take a step to re-sync the map.\n") else cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> mapper <yellow>off<reset> " .. "\226\128\148 the map is frozen (nothing added, nothing moved); " .. "<yellow>mapper on<reset> to resume.\n") end end
-- `mapper outworld [full|roads|off]` — how much of the outworld grid -- gets mapped; the bare form reports the current mode. Only affects -- NEW tiles: existing ones stay on the map and still recenter. function icesus.mapper.outworldCommand(arg) if arg == "full" or arg == "roads" or arg == "off" then icesus.settings = icesus.settings or {} icesus.settings.outworldMode = arg icesus.saveSettings() -- Back to full: every tile maps again, so the position cursor -- has no job left — drop it rather than leave a stray '@' cell. if arg == "full" and icesus.mapper.idMap then local cur = icesus.mapper.idMap.cursorRoom if cur and deleteRoom then pcall(deleteRoom, cur) end icesus.mapper.idMap.cursorRoom = nil end local desc = { full = "every tile is mapped (the default)", roads = "roads, paths, mine entrances and buildings are added " .. "\226\128\148 a lean ridable atlas; bulk terrain " .. "(forest, plains, water\226\128\166) is ignored, and " .. "Default Area strays are pruned as you ride over them", off = "no new outworld tiles are added; indoor zones still map", } cecho(string.format("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> outworld mapping " .. "<yellow>%s<reset> \226\128\148 %s. Tiles already mapped stay " .. "put (<yellow>mapper reset<reset> to rebuild lean from " .. "scratch).\n", arg, desc[arg])) else local mode = (icesus.settings and icesus.settings.outworldMode) or "full" cecho(string.format( "\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> outworld mapping is <yellow>%s<reset> " .. "(<yellow>mapper outworld full|roads|off<reset> to change).\n", mode)) end end
-- `mapper autosave [on|off]` — the bare form reports the current mode. function icesus.mapper.autosaveCommand(arg) if arg == "on" then icesus.mapper.setSaveMode("auto") elseif arg == "off" then icesus.mapper.setSaveMode("manual") else local mode = (icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapSaveMode) or "auto" cecho(string.format( "\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> map autosave is <yellow>%s<reset> " .. "(<yellow>mapper autosave on|off<reset> to change).\n", mode == "auto" and "on" or "off")) end end
-- Save cadence. Two modes, toggled with `mapper autosave on|off` or -- the HUD mode pill (persisted via icesus.settings): -- -- auto (default) — v1.0.14 behaviour: the map is flushed to disk -- only when the player goes quiet, never mid-walk or mid-fight, -- where a full saveMap on a large accumulated map stutters the -- client (issue #4). A hard cap still guarantees a flush during a -- very long unbroken session. Idle-deferral approach and -- thresholds contributed by Steve De Jongh (sdejongh / Arthr). -- -- manual — no timed saves at all: the player flushes via -- `mapper save` or the HUD badge. A throttled console reminder -- fires in quiet moments once changes get old. Both modes still -- flush on exit, disconnect and package teardown. local IDLE_SAVE_SECS = 10 -- flush this long after the last move/fight local MAX_SAVE_SECS = 300 -- ...but never hold unsaved changes longer local SAVE_POLL_SECS = 5 -- how often the idle check runs local REMIND_SECS = 900 -- manual mode: nag at most this often
-- Mark "the player is doing something" so the idle timer holds off. -- Called on every Room.Info (walking) and while Char.Status reports -- combat. os.time()'s 1s resolution is plenty for a 10s threshold. function icesus.mapper.touchActivity() icesus.mapper.lastActivity = os.time() end
-- Decide whether now is a good moment to flush. No-op unless the map -- is dirty. Auto mode: flush once the player has been idle for -- IDLE_SAVE_SECS and isn't fighting, or unconditionally once the map -- has been dirty for MAX_SAVE_SECS regardless of what they're doing. -- Manual mode: never flush — just emit the throttled reminder. function icesus.mapper.maybeFlush() if not icesus.mapper.dirty then return end local now = os.time() local idle_for = now - (icesus.mapper.lastActivity or 0) local in_combat = icesus.state and icesus.state.inCombat
-- Manual mode: never save on a timer. Once the oldest unsaved change -- is REMIND_SECS old, drop a single console reminder in a quiet -- moment, throttled to one per REMIND_SECS. if icesus.settings and icesus.settings.mapSaveMode == "manual" then local dirty_for = now - (icesus.mapper.dirtySince or now) local last_nag = now - (icesus.mapper.lastRemind or 0) if dirty_for >= REMIND_SECS and last_nag >= REMIND_SECS and not in_combat and idle_for >= IDLE_SAVE_SECS then icesus.mapper.lastRemind = now local n = icesus.mapper.dirtyCount or 0 cecho(string.format( "\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> %d map change%s not saved yet " .. "\226\128\148 <yellow>mapper save<reset> (or click the map " .. "badge) when convenient.\n", n, n == 1 and "" or "s")) end return end
local since_save = now - (icesus.mapper.lastSave or 0) if since_save >= MAX_SAVE_SECS or (not in_combat and idle_for >= IDLE_SAVE_SECS) then icesus.mapper.flushSave() end end
-- Self-re-arming idle poll. Replaces the old fixed 30s "flush + re-run -- the whole install path" timer, which saved on a blind cadence even -- mid-walk / mid-combat. function icesus.mapper.startSaveTimer() if icesus.mapper.saveTimer then pcall(killTimer, icesus.mapper.saveTimer) end if not tempTimer then return end icesus.mapper.saveTimer = tempTimer(SAVE_POLL_SECS, function() icesus.mapper.maybeFlush() icesus.mapper.startSaveTimer() end) end
function icesus.mapper.reset(silent) -- deleteMap() is the obvious choice but it leaves Mudlet's player- -- room pointer dangling and the next centerview() segfaults the -- whole client. Walk our own idToRoom and delete rooms one at a -- time instead — slower but stable. if icesus.mapper.idMap and deleteRoom then for _, rid in pairs(icesus.mapper.idMap.idToRoom or {}) do pcall(deleteRoom, rid) end if icesus.mapper.idMap.cursorRoom then pcall(deleteRoom, icesus.mapper.idMap.cursorRoom) end end -- Drop the areas we created, now that they're empty. Without this a -- reset leaves the full area list in the map with nothing in it — the -- "all the area names are populated from start, even with an empty -- map" half of issue #12. Anything that still holds rooms (a room the -- player made, or one of ours we somehow missed) is left alone, and -- areas we never created are never touched. if deleteArea and icesus.mapper.idMap then for _, aid in pairs(icesus.mapper.idMap.areaToInt or {}) do local empty = true if getAreaRooms then local ok, list = pcall(getAreaRooms, aid) if ok and type(list) == "table" and next(list) ~= nil then empty = false end end if empty then pcall(deleteArea, aid) end end end if os.remove then pcall(os.remove, mapDataPath()) end if os.remove then pcall(os.remove, idMapPath()) end icesus.mapper.idMap = { idToRoom = {}, areaToInt = {}, placed = {}, gridmoded = {}, areaCoords = {}, seen = {}, next_id = 1, } icesus.mapper.lastHexId = nil icesus.mapper.dirty = false icesus.mapper.dirtyCount = 0 icesus.mapper.dirtySince = nil if icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI then pcall(icesus.mapper.refreshSaveUI) end if updateMap then pcall(updateMap) end if not silent then cecho("\n<lime_green>Icesus<reset> mapper reset \226\128\148 the next room you enter will start a fresh map.\n") end end
-- Detect a stale idMap: idToRoom references rooms that Mudlet no longer -- knows about (e.g. player deleted the map via Mudlet's UI). Without -- this check, addRoom() short-circuits forever because every hexId -- maps to an integer that isn't a real Mudlet room, and the player -- "can't recreate the map" until they discover `mapper reset`. local function idMapIsStale(m) if not m or not m.idToRoom or not getRoomName then return false end local sampled, missing = 0, 0 for _, rid in pairs(m.idToRoom) do sampled = sampled + 1 local ok, name = pcall(getRoomName, rid) if not ok or name == nil or name == "" then missing = missing + 1 end if sampled >= 5 then break end end -- All sampled rooms gone = Mudlet's map was wiped externally. return sampled > 0 and missing == sampled end
function icesus.mapper.install() -- Restore persisted state up front so the player's existing map -- shows in F11 even before any Room.Info arrives this session. if not icesus.mapper.idMap then -- Crash-loop guard. The sentinel only survives on disk if the -- previous session died between writing it and removing it a few -- lines further down — i.e. inside loadMap, which runs in Mudlet -- C++ where pcall can't help (a segfault on a bad .dat, or the -- player force-quitting a frozen load). Reloading the same file -- would kill every login the same way, so boot WITHOUT it this -- session: the files stay untouched on disk, the client comes -- up, and the player decides — walk on (the map rebuilds as they -- go) or roll back with `mapper restore`. local skipLoad = false if io.exists and io.exists(sentinelPath()) then pcall(os.remove, sentinelPath()) skipLoad = true -- Snapshot the pair before this session can touch it. A recovery -- boot is the one case where we neither load the .dat nor check -- it against the engine, so whatever map Mudlet auto-loaded runs -- the session and gets flushed over the file at the end — and if -- that copy was older, the newer one is gone. The files are still -- intact right here; a forced backup makes the newer map a -- `mapper restore` away no matter what happens next. makeBackup(true) cecho("\n<red>Icesus<reset> the last session died while loading " .. "the map, so the map file was skipped this session to let " .. "you back in. <yellow>mapper restore<reset> lists backups " .. "if the map file itself is at fault.\n") end icesus.mapper.idMap = loadIdMap() local m = icesus.mapper.idMap -- Skip the .dat when the engine already holds the same generation -- of our map (reloading over a populated map freezes Mudlet for -- minutes on big maps). Also skip on a fresh profile: Mudlet logs -- a noisy "Unable to open map file for reading" + debug dump when -- the file is missing, and pcall doesn't suppress it (the message -- is emitted from Mudlet C++, not raised as a Lua error). local doLoad = not skipLoad and loadMap and io.exists and io.exists(mapDataPath()) if doLoad then local known, live = engineCoverage(m) if known > 0 and live >= known * MAP_FRESH_RATIO then doLoad = false -- same generation, nothing to do elseif live > 0 then -- Ours, but short: Mudlet auto-loaded an older copy of the map -- than the .dat the idmap was saved with. Loading straight on -- top would make the engine tear every colliding room down one -- at a time; clear our own rooms first, the way restore does, -- and warn, because on a big map this is the slow path. cecho(string.format( "\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> the map Mudlet loaded is behind your " .. "saved one (%d of %d rooms) \226\128\148 reloading from " .. "<yellow>Icesus.map.dat<reset>. Mudlet may freeze for a bit " .. "on a large map; let it finish.\n", live, known)) if deleteRoom then for _, rid in pairs(m.idToRoom or {}) do pcall(deleteRoom, rid) end if m.cursorRoom then pcall(deleteRoom, m.cursorRoom) end end m.cursorRoom = nil end end if doLoad then local sf = io.open(sentinelPath(), "w") if sf then sf:write("loading") sf:close() end pcall(loadMap, mapDataPath()) -- Re-seed next_id now that the engine knows the .dat's rooms — -- loadIdMap ran before the load, so its collision guard was -- blind to them. if createRoomID then local ok, v = pcall(createRoomID) if ok and type(v) == "number" then m.next_id = math.max(m.next_id or 1, v) end end pcall(os.remove, sentinelPath()) end -- Stale detection also runs on the sentinel-recovery path. It has -- to: with the map deliberately not loaded AND the engine empty, -- the idmap really is orphaned for this session, and keeping it -- would leave flushSave's wipe guard refusing every save until the -- player restarts — a whole session of walking, mapped and thrown -- away, while the console told them to walk on and rebuild. -- Quarantining hands them a writable slate and keeps the old pair -- (plus every backup) for `mapper restore`. If the engine did come -- up with our rooms, idMapIsStale is false and nothing happens. if idMapIsStale(m) then cecho("\n<yellow>Icesus<reset> mapper detected a wiped Mudlet map " .. "\226\128\148 clearing stale room IDs so the next room you " .. "enter starts a fresh map. The old files were set aside as " .. ".bad-* in the profile folder, and <yellow>mapper " .. "restore<reset> lists your backups.\n") -- Quarantine before the reset so the automatic path never -- destroys data — reset()'s os.remove then finds nothing. -- Only the player's explicit `mapper reset` truly deletes. quarantineLivePair() icesus.mapper.reset(true) end end setupTerrainEnvs() -- Seed the save clock so the cap measures from boot, then start the -- idle-aware flush poll. Saving is deferred to quiet moments now -- (see icesus.mapper.maybeFlush) so walking and combat stay fluid. local boot = os.time() icesus.mapper.lastActivity = boot icesus.mapper.lastSave = boot icesus.mapper.startSaveTimer() end
function icesus.mapper.teardown() if icesus.mapper.saveTimer then pcall(killTimer, icesus.mapper.saveTimer) icesus.mapper.saveTimer = nil end icesus.mapper.flushSave() icesus.mapper.booted = nil -- next install() will re-boot on Char.Base end
